title: Healthcare POC — privacy-first quant & prompt pipeline notes
content:
Context and goal:
- Customer: mid-sized digital health platform (HIPAA scope). Goal: deploy a clinical summarization and triage assistant in a VPC/on-prem config with strict PHI handling and 99th percentile latency < 300ms for 512-token outputs.

High-level constraints:
- No PHI leaves customer network; private control plane + HSM/KMS integration required.
- Hard latency targets for the triage fast-path (diagnostic classification) vs more relaxed for full-note summarization.
- Cost sensitivity: customer prefers dedicated reserved capacity to avoid spike pricing.

Key design patterns we are evaluating:
1) Privacy-first inference pipeline (preferred):
   - On-prem model serving inside VPC. All requests redacted by a local preprocessor using regex + ML entity detector. Redaction log stored locally; only redaction hashes (non-reversible) sent to telemetry.
   - Two-stage cascade: small classifier -> mid-size summarizer; classifier runs on a quantized 4-bit model for ~30ms inference, summarizer on 8-bit quantized 13B for better quality.
   - Fallback policy: if classifier confidence low or explicit PHI tokens detected, route to human-in-loop queue.

2) Hybrid routing with hosted fallback (only for non-PHI):
   - When requests are labelled non-PHI and meet routing policy (low latency but low-cost), route to hosted Mistral-like instance with strict model pin to verified version. Otherwise stay on dedicated.

Model candidates & rationale:
- Small classifier options (cheap low-latency): Distil-family / 1-3B distilled Llama variants -> tradeoff: fastest in int4 but lower recall on rare clinical terms.
- Mid-sized summarizer (quality sweet spot): Llama-2-13B, Mistral-7B-Instruct, Falcon-7B-Instruct. Quantization candidates: int8 for Llama-2-13B (more memory but stable FP fallback), int4 for Mistral-7B (smaller, faster).
- High-quality fallback: Llama-2-70B or equivalent only for offline batch review or paid escalation. Not in initial POC.

Quantization experiments (notes from lab run 2024-11-25):
- Setup: Dedicated 1xA10G node, sequence length 512 (avg), batch size 4 small inference jobs, single-threaded baseline and Redwood runtime with batching enabled.
- Models/variants tried: Llama-2-13B (fp16, int8), Mistral-7B (fp16, int4), distilled-3B (int4).
- Observed median token latency (generation-only):
   * Llama-2-13B fp16: 180ms/token (cold), 120ms/token (warm with KV cache)
   * Llama-2-13B int8: 120ms/token (cold), 85ms/token (warm) — good stability, slight quality drop on numeric tables in notes
   * Mistral-7B fp16: 110ms/token (cold), 70ms/token (warm)
   * Mistral-7B int4: 65ms/token (cold), 45ms/token (warm) — hallucination noise increased on medication lists
   * Distilled-3B int4 classifier: 12–18ms per request (inference only)
- Cost-performance note: int4 Mistral gave best latency but had an increased rate of entity hallucination in clinical passages (safety concern). Int8 Llama-2-13B appeared to offer the best tradeoff for summarization quality vs cost given customer's risk tolerance.

Prompting and pipeline tuning (empirical notes):
- Redaction-first prompt: always prepend a sanitized block showing what was redacted and the count of redact types. This helps model keep context on omissions and reduces invented PHI. Example prepend snippet used in tests: "REDACTED_ENTITIES: [DATE:x, NAME:y, ID:z]; CONTEXT: patient visit notes."
- System role annotations: explicit instruction to never fabricate dates, names, or identifiers; include a firm "IF YOU CANNOT ANSWER, SAY 'UNABLE_TO_SUMMARIZE_DUE_TO_PHRASE'" clause to reduce confident hallucinations.
- Few-shot examples: include 6 examples with both redacted and non-redacted variants to teach the model how to summarize while not replacing redacted tokens.
- Temperature & decoding: use deterministic decoding (temperature=0.0) for classifier & triage outputs; sampling (temp 0.2–0.4) for human-friendly narrative summaries when allowed.

Caching and batching heuristics for SLOs:
- KV cache warm-up policy: keep hot conversation KV in memory for 15 minutes after last use for triage sessions. This reduces warm latency 30–40% in our runs.
- Dynamic batching thresholds: prefer small batches (2–8) for triage classifier to keep p95 under 300ms; larger batches acceptable for background summarization jobs.

Eval plan and metrics (POC scope):
- Safety/PHI metrics: redaction recall, false-redaction rate, instances of invented PHI flagged by reviewer. Target: redaction recall >= 99%, invented-PHI incidents <= 0.1% of outputs.
- Quality: ROUGE-L and clinician-rated utility score (1–5). Target: median clinician utility >= 4 for summarizer.
- Latency: median and p95 generation latency for 512 tokens; target p95 < 300ms for triage classifier path.
- Cost: tokens per summary, cost per 1000 summaries vs baseline.

Decision log (working):
- 2024-11-20: agreed to prioritize privacy-first on-prem design for initial pilot. (Aisha)
- 2024-11-25: int4 Mistral too risky due to hallucinated medications — pivot to int8 Llama-2-13B for summarizer. (Marco)
- 2024-11-27: add preprocessor entity confidence threshold; below threshold send to HITL. (Riley)

Open questions / risks:
- Quantization library compatibility with HSM/KMS enclaves — does the runtime support loading quantized kernels inside our customer's FIPS environment? Need security to validate.
- Long-tail clinical vocabulary: small classifier misses rare disease names; consider augmenting training with customer-specific lexicon or lexicon-based recall patch.
- Observability: build per-token hallucination detector hooks into Redwood Console to raise regression alerts during rollout.

Short-term action items (next 2 sprints):
- [ ] Run expanded eval with 2500 deidentified notes from customer to validate invented-PHI rate (owner: Riley, due 2024-12-10).
- [ ] Prototype entity lexicon augmentor in preprocessor and re-run classifier recall tests (owner: Marco, due 2024-12-05).
- [ ] Security review of quantized model runtime inside customer VPC + HSM (owner: Sofia, due 2024-12-08).
- [ ] Integrate explicit fail-open human-in-loop queue in the Redwood routing policy for low confidence / PHI cases (owner: Aisha, due 2024-12-03).

Notes to self / rough ideas for later:
- Investigate prefix-tuning rather than full quantized fp16 for summarizer to reduce memory footprint while preserving quality.
- Experiment with constrained decoding conditioned on a structured template to reduce free-form hallucinations in medication lists.

Slack + resources referenced during testing:
- #se-healthcare-poc thread (link in Confluence doc).
- PR with model packaging changes: github.com/redwood-inference/poctools/pull/89

Meeting frag notes (2024-12-02 sync):
- Customer asked for an offline audit of any redaction decisions; propose weekly artifact bundle export.
- Customer accepts slight quality hit if it improves safety and PHI guarantees.
- Next demo planned 2024-12-12: show classifier latency and three sanitized summaries.

Bottom line (working recommendation):
- For this POC, pursue an on-prem privacy-first pipeline with a quantization mix: int4 classifiers for triage where possible, int8 13B summarizer for production summaries. Emphasize strict preprocessing redaction + HITL for ambiguous cases.

-- end of notes (draft)
